# iliad-019 (3.264–368) — new renderings

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἵπποι ἀερσίποδες (3.327) | "the foot-lifting horses" | "high-stepping horses" (+ note: usual explanation, sense not quite certain) | "swift-footed" (reserved for ποδάρκης / ποδώκης), "prancing", "tall", "high-hoofed"; ἀείρω "lift" + πούς "foot" |
| ποικίλα τεύχεα (3.327) | "intricate armour" | "intricate armour" | "dappled", "many-coloured", "inlaid" (reserved for ποικίλος of wood and metal work in the Odyssey table, but armour here is not said to be inlaid); extends the Odyssey table’s ποικίλος "intricate" to τεύχεα "armour" |
| τιμὴν … ἀποτινέμεν · τιμὴν … τίνειν (3.286, 3.288) | "a recompense … to pay back" · "the recompense … to pay" | "a recompense" · "the recompense" | "honour" (the Odyssey table’s τιμή, and the Iliad’s τιμὴν ἀρνύμενοι, 1.159, "winning honour"; here the word names something paid, so "to pay honour" would mislead), "price", "fine", "penalty", "indemnity"; a departure from the Odyssey table, with the reason, and the note says τιμή is the price paid for a wrong |
| ποινή (εἵνεκα ποινῆς, 3.290) | "requital" | "requital" | "blood-price", "vengeance" (reserved for τίνομαι "take vengeance"), "payment"; kept apart from ἄποινα "ransom" (1.13) and from τιμή above |
| ὅρκια πιστὰ θεῶν σύναγον (3.269) | "the faithful oaths of the gods brought together" | "brought together the faithful oaths of the gods" | "gathered", "oath-offerings"; the line follows iliad-018’s κήρυκες … φέρον ὅρκια πιστά (3.245) and the table’s ὅρκια πιστά "faithful oaths" |
| κήρυκες ἀγαυοί (3.268) | "the heralds, noble ones" | "the noble heralds" | "illustrious", "proud", "splendid" (ἀγλαός); follows the shipped odyssey-037 "noble heralds" |
| Ἴδηθεν μεδέων (3.276 = 3.320, whole half-line address) | "from Ida ruling" | "you who rule from Ida" | "lord of Ida" (the noun μέδων is "lord", but this is the participle), "reigning from Ida", "watching over Ida" (μέδω "rule"); -θεν "from" |
| Ζεῦ πάτερ … κύδιστε μέγιστε (3.276, 3.298, 3.320) | "Father Zeus … most glorious, greatest" | "Father Zeus … most glorious, greatest" | "most renowned", "highest" (reserved for ὕπατος), "greatest of all"; κύδιστε keeps the Iliad’s "most glorious" (1.122), and the pair is the same in all three prayers |
| Ἠέλιός θ’, ὃς πάντ’ ἐφορᾷ καὶ πάντ’ ἐπακούεις (3.277, second person) | "and Sun, you who oversee all things and listen to all things" | "and Sun, you who see everything and hear everything" | "all-seeing", "all-hearing" (compresses the two verbs); the Odyssey’s half-line in the third person (11.109), changed only for the person |
| καμόντας ἀνθρώπους (3.278–279) | "men who have toiled" | "men whose toil is done" (+ note: the dead) | "weary men", "the dead" (decides the euphemism), "men who have laboured"; follows the Odyssey’s φθιμένων / καμόντων row "mortals who have toiled" / "whose toil is done" |
| ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσῃ (3.279) | "swears a false oath" | "swears a false oath" | "swears falsely", "breaks his oath" (breaks is πημαίνω ὑπὲρ ὅρκια, 3.299), "perjures himself"; ἐπίορκον is the adjective, "false oath" |
| ὑμεῖς μάρτυροι ἔστε, φυλάσσετε δ’ ὅρκια πιστά (3.280) | "you be witnesses, and guard the faithful oaths" | "be witnesses, and guard the faithful oaths" | "witness this", "watch over", "keep"; φυλάσσω "guard" |
| Ζεῦ ἄνα (3.351) | "Zeus, lord" | "Lord Zeus" | "O king Zeus", "Zeus, my lord"; follows the shipped odyssey-085 |
| ποντοπόροισιν (νήεσσι ποντοπόροισιν, 3.283) | "in our sea-crossing ships" | "in our sea-crossing ships" | the table’s ποντοπόρος "sea-crossing" (2.771, 3.240), unchanged |
| ξανθὸς Μενέλαος (3.284) | "fair-haired Menelaus" | "fair-haired Menelaus" | Odyssey table, unchanged |
| ἀποδοῦναι · ἀποτινέμεν (infinitives of command, 3.285–286) | "are to give back" · "to pay back" | "are to give … back" · "to pay" | "must", "shall" (not in the Greek); the infinitive stands for an imperative and the English supplies "are to" once for the pair |
| ἥ τε καὶ ἐσσομένοισι μετ’ ἀνθρώποισι πέληται (3.287) | "which shall be among men yet to come as well" | "one that will remain among men yet to come as well" | "which shall be remembered" (decides the sense), "which shall be a lesson"; ἐσσόμενοι keeps the table’s "those yet to come" |
| εἵνεκα ποινῆς αὖθι μένων, ἧός κε τέλος πολέμοιο κιχείω (3.290–291) | "for the sake of the requital, staying here, until I find the end of the war" | "for the sake of the requital, staying here until I find the end of the war" | "reach" (the table turns it down for κιχάνω, "found" at 19.400), "see", "come to"; τέλος "end" |
| ἦ, καί (3.292) | "He spoke, and" | "So he said, and" | the table’s ἦ καί, unchanged |
| νηλέϊ χαλκῷ (3.292) | "pitiless bronze" | "the pitiless bronze" | Odyssey table, unchanged |
| στομάχους … τάμε (3.292) | "the throats … he cut off" | "cut … throats" | "gullets", "slit"; ἀπὸ … τάμνω "cut off" in tmesis |
| ἀσπαίροντας θυμοῦ δευομένους (3.293–294) | "gasping, lacking life" | "gasping, lacking life" | "bereft of breath", "short of life", "breathing their last"; θυμός of the life that leaves the body is "life", δεύομαι "lack" (1.602) |
| ἀπὸ γὰρ μένος εἵλετο χαλκός (3.294) | "for the bronze took their might away" | "for the bronze took their might away" | "strength" (reserved for κράτος / σθένος), "fury", "spirit"; μένος keeps the table’s "might" |
| ὧδε δέ τις εἴπεσκεν Ἀχαιῶν τε Τρώων τε (3.297 = 3.319, whole-line speech introduction) | "And thus kept saying someone of the Achaeans and of the Trojans:" | "And thus would some man, Achaean or Trojan, say:" | "one after another", "each man in turn" (adds), "said"; -σκ- iterative shown by "kept" in `l` and "would" in `i` |
| ὁππότεροι πρότεροι ὑπὲρ ὅρκια πημήνειαν (3.299) | "whichever of the two first, in breach of the oaths, do harm" | "whichever side first does harm in breach of the oaths" | "break the oaths" (πημαίνω is "do harm"), "transgress" (the Odyssey’s ὑπερβασίη "overstepping"), "wrong"; ὑπέρ "over, beyond" |
| ὧδέ σφ’ ἐγκέφαλος χαμάδις ῥέοι ὡς ὅδε οἶνος (3.300) | "so may their brain flow to the ground, like this wine" | "may their brain run out on the ground like this wine" | "may their brains be spilled", "pour out"; ἐγκέφαλος "brain" (singular), "to the ground" as the Odyssey’s ἐγκέφαλος … χαμάδις "the brain ... onto the ground" |
| ἄλοχοι δ’ ἄλλοισι δαμεῖεν (3.301) | "their wives be subdued to others" | "may their wives be made subject to other men" | "be taken by others", "be violated" (names what the verb leaves open), "be enslaved" (adds); δάμνημι "subdue" and the shipped "made subject" (3.183) |
| ὣς ἔφαν, οὐδ’ ἄρα πώ σφιν ἐπεκραίαινε Κρονίων (3.302) | "So they spoke, but not yet for them did the son of Cronus bring it to fulfilment" | "So they spoke, but the son of Cronus did not yet fulfil it for them" | "grant" (reserved for δίδωμι), "answer"; the 2.419 row (ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἄρα πώ οἱ ἐπεκραίαινε Κρονίων) with the plural speaker and pronoun, as the table does for ὣς ἔφαν |
| Δαρδανίδης Πρίαμος (3.303) | "Dardanus’ descendant Priam" | "Priam, a descendant of Dardanus" | "Dardanus’ son", "the Dardanian"; a descendant, not a son, as the table’s ποδώκης Αἰακίδης "descendant of Aeacus" |
| τοῖσι δὲ Δαρδανίδης Πρίαμος μετὰ μῦθον ἔειπε (3.303, whole-line speech introduction) | "And among them Dardanus’ descendant Priam a speech spoke:" | "And Priam, a descendant of Dardanus, spoke among them:" | "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη), "answered"; the Odyssey table’s μετὰ μῦθον ἔειπον "among them a speech I spoke" / "I spoke among them" for a named third person |
| ἤτοι ἐγών (3.305) | "For my part, I" | "For my part, I" | "Truly I", "I indeed", "I for one"; ἤτοι is one word in the edition, and the Odyssey table’s ἤτοι "he then" is not the sense here |
| οὔ πω τλήσομ’ … ὁρᾶσθαι (3.306) | "by no means shall I endure to look" | "I shall by no means endure to look" | "I cannot bring myself to" (the table’s τλάω for "bring oneself" is for the aorist, 11.350), "I could not bear", "never will I"; τλάω "endure" |
| Ζεὺς μέν που τό γε οἶδε (3.308) | "Zeus doubtless this at least knows" | "Zeus doubtless knows this" | "perhaps", "I suppose", "somewhere"; που "doubtless", as the shipped odyssey-067 |

| ἀνασχόμενος (3.362) | "raising himself" | "rising to the blow" | "lifting his arm", "drawing back", "gathering himself"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀνασχόμενος "raising himself" / "rising to the blow" (odyssey-070) |
| κόρυθος φάλον (3.362; φάλος, usual explanation: the ridge of the helmet, sense not certain) | "the ridge of the helmet" | "the ridge of the helmet" (+ note: sense not certain) | "boss", "crest" (kept for λόφος), "plate", "horn" (each decides the unknown); κόρυς keeps "helmet" |
| ἀμφὶ δ’ ἄρ’ αὐτῷ τριχθά τε καὶ τετραχθὰ διατρυφὲν ἔκπεσε χειρός (3.362–363) | "and about it in three pieces and in four, shattered, it fell from his hand" | "and around it the sword was shattered into three pieces and four and fell from his hand" | "in three and four pieces" alone, "into fragments", "in many pieces"; the idiom keeps both numbers, and αὐτῷ is read as the helmet, as the note says |
| ᾤμωξεν (3.364) | "wailed" | "cried out" | "groaned" (reserved for στενάχω), "moaned", "shrieked"; follows the Odyssey’s οἰμώζω "groaned … cried out" in odyssey-043 and odyssey-060 |
| εἰς οὐρανὸν εὐρύν (3.364) | "to the wide heaven" | "up to the wide heaven" | "to the broad sky", "wide sky"; εὐρύς "wide" (1.478) and the Odyssey’s "wide heaven" |
| Ζεῦ πάτερ, οὔ τις σεῖο θεῶν ὀλοώτερος ἄλλος (3.365, speech opening) | Odyssey wording: "“Father Zeus, none of the gods is deadlier than you, none other;" | Odyssey wording: "“Father Zeus, no other god is deadlier than you;" | the unit takes the Odyssey’s English whole, with the opening quotation mark added; the validator therefore warns that the English differs from odyssey-100 (the mark is the only difference) |
| ἦ τ’ ἐφάμην τίσασθαι Ἀλέξανδρον κακότητος (3.366) | "Truly I thought to take vengeance on Alexander for his baseness" | "Truly I thought I would take vengeance on Alexander for his baseness" | "I was sure", "I swore" (φημί "say, think"), "wickedness", "misdeed" (κακότης keeps the Iliad’s "baseness", 2.368) |
| νῦν δέ μοι ἐν χείρεσσιν ἄγη ξίφος (3.367) | "but now in my hands my sword is broken" | "but now my sword is broken in my hands" | "shattered" (reserved for διατρυφέν), "snapped", "has broken" in `l`; ἄγνυμι "break" |
| ἐκ δέ μοι ἔγχος ἠΐχθη παλάμηφιν ἐτώσιον (3.367–368) | "and from me the spear darted from my palm in vain" | "and my spear darted from my palm in vain" | "flew", "sped", "leapt" (each decides the force), "to no purpose" (the Odyssey’s αὔτως `i`), "uselessly"; ἀΐσσω "dart", ἐτώσιον "in vain" (an adverb), παλάμηφιν "from my palm" |
| οὐδ’ ἔβαλόν μιν (3.368) | "and I did not hit him" | "and I did not hit him" | "wound", "strike", "touch"; βάλλω of a weapon is "hit" |
